nodes.What it is: A robot is a set of rigid parts, and every part gets its own coordinate frame. Rotation matrices, quaternions and 4x4 homogeneous transforms convert a point from one frame to another. Almost every robotics bug starts with a wrong frame or a wrong rotation convention.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mature textbook material. The modern teaching standard (Modern Robotics) uses Lie groups SO(3)/SE(3) and twists. Tooling (Robotics Toolbox for Python, Pinocchio) makes transforms one-liners.

nodes.What it is: A robot description file lists the links (with masses, inertias and meshes) and joints (type, axis, limits) of a robot. URDF is the ROS standard and MJCF is MuJoCo's format. Simulators, IK solvers and dynamics libraries all read these files, so a wrong file breaks everything downstream.
nodes.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; XML; basic CAD helps
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Curated model libraries (MuJoCo Menagerie) ship ready-made arms, quadrupeds and humanoids; CAD-to-robot exporters (onshape-to-robot) produce URDF/SDF/MJCF directly from Onshape assemblies, including kinematic loops.
nodes.Key players: Google DeepMind (MuJoCo, Menagerie), Rhoban/Bordeaux (onshape-to-robot), ROS community

nodes.What it is: Forward kinematics computes where the robot's hand (end-effector) is, given all joint angles. It chains one transform per joint. The two classic recipes are Denavit-Hartenberg parameters and the product-of-exponentials formula.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Solved for serial arms; still the first building block for every controller, IK solver and learned policy that outputs end-effector poses.
nodes.Key players: Modern Robotics authors; Springer Handbook ch. 2 (Waldron & Schmiedeler); Stanford CS223A

nodes.What it is: The Jacobian is a matrix that maps joint speeds to the hand's linear and angular speed, and joint torques to hand forces. At a singularity the Jacobian loses rank: the arm cannot move in some direction no matter how fast the joints spin. Manipulability measures how close the arm is to that.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Standard theory; current tools compute Jacobians, Hessians and manipulability automatically, and differential-IK libraries use them in real time.
nodes.Key players: Stanford CS223A (Khatib), Modern Robotics, QUT Robotics Toolbox

nodes.What it is: Inverse kinematics (IK) answers the reverse question: which joint angles put the hand at a target pose? Simple arms have closed-form formulas; general arms need iterative numerical solvers that respect joint limits. There can be zero, one or many solutions.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Numerical IK is commodity (TRAC-IK combines Newton and SQP solvers to handle joint limits). The open part is speed and robustness for many-DoF robots and many simultaneous goals.

nodes.What it is: Instead of solving IK once, differential IK computes at every control step a small joint velocity that moves the robot toward several goals at once (hand pose, posture, center of mass) while respecting limits. It is written as a small quadratic program. Robots with more joints than needed (redundant) use the extra freedom for secondary goals.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Task-based QP IK is now the default for teleoperation, humanoid retargeting and whole-body motion. mink handles floating bases and collision limits; Pink does the same on Pinocchio models.

nodes.What it is: Wheeled robots cannot slide sideways, which is a 'nonholonomic' constraint. Differential-drive, unicycle and car-like robots share one simple model that turns wheel speeds into forward speed and turning rate. Integrating this model from wheel encoders gives odometry.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mature; used everywhere in AMRs and mobile manipulators. Remaining difficulty is wheel slip, which kinematics alone does not model.
nodes.Key players: Modern Robotics ch. 13, Caltech, ROS navigation community

nodes.What it is: In a parallel robot (e.g. a delta robot), several legs connect the base to the moving platform, forming closed loops. For these, inverse kinematics is often easy and forward kinematics is hard, the reverse of serial arms. Closed loops also appear inside legs and grippers (linkages).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Closed-loop support is now native in dynamics libraries (Pinocchio) and CAD exporters (onshape-to-robot closing constraints). Accurate simulation of many coupled loops with contacts is still an active topic.
nodes.Key players: Pinocchio team (Inria), simulation researchers; open-source delta builders

nodes.What it is: Dynamics links motion to forces: the mass matrix M(q), Coriolis/centrifugal terms and gravity give tau = M(q)q'' + C(q,q')q' + g(q). Inverse dynamics computes the torques needed for a desired motion; forward dynamics computes the motion produced by given torques. This is what physics simulators integrate every step.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Classical theory (Lagrange, Newton-Euler, Featherstone's spatial algebra). Taught in MIT Underactuated and Stanford CS223A; underlies all model-based control and simulation.
nodes.Key players: Roy Featherstone, David Orin (Springer Handbook ch. 3), MIT (Tedrake), Stanford (Khatib)

nodes.What it is: Recursive algorithms (RNEA for inverse dynamics, ABA for forward dynamics) compute dynamics in time linear in the number of joints. Modern libraries also compute their exact derivatives, which gradient-based optimizers and MPC need.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Pinocchio (Inria Paris, BSD) provides analytical derivatives of RNEA/ABA, centroidal dynamics, closed loops and frictional contact solvers; it powers Crocoddyl and many humanoid MPC stacks.

nodes.What it is: A path says where to go; a trajectory also says when. Time scaling assigns speeds along a path so velocity, acceleration and jerk limits are respected. Jerk-limited (S-curve) profiles make motion smooth and protect hardware.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Real-time jerk-limited generators (Ruckig, <1 ms) and time-optimal path parameterization (TOPP-RA) are mature and used in MoveIt. Active work: combining with collision-aware planners and learned policies' outputs.

nodes.What it is: Identification estimates the real masses, inertias and friction of a robot from recorded motion and torque/current data, because CAD values are wrong. For cheap servos, the friction and motor model often matter more than link inertias. Good identified models shrink the sim-to-real gap.
nodes.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; least squares; logging data from motors
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Physically consistent identification (SDP constraints) is standard in research (BIRDy benchmark). Rhoban's BAM (2024-26) fits extended friction models for common servos (Dynamixel, eRob and the SO-101's Feetech STS3215) and plugs into MuJoCo/mjlab for RL sim-to-real.

nodes.What it is: Real robots differ from their URDF by small errors in link lengths and joint offsets. Kinematic calibration measures the robot in many poses and corrects these parameters; hand-eye calibration finds where the camera is relative to the robot. Both are needed before a camera-guided arm can hit a target.
nodes.Prerequisites: Forward kinematics; least squares; camera basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Recent work removes markers and external sensors, calibrating arm and RGB-D camera together from learned image correspondences (RA-L 2025).
nodes.Key players: Industrial metrology vendors (not mapped here), academic calibration groups

nodes.What it is: Legged robots and humanoids are not bolted to the ground: their base is a free 6-DoF body that moves only through contact forces. Centroidal dynamics summarizes the whole robot by its center of mass and momentum, which makes balance and jumping tractable. Optimal control libraries plan whole-body motions with these models.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Whole-body trajectory optimization and MPC (Crocoddyl, built on Pinocchio) handle multi-contact plans; in 2025-26 these models are often combined with RL tracking policies on low-cost humanoids such as Unitree G1.
nodes.Key players: LAAS-CNRS / Heriot-Watt (Edinburgh Centre for Robotics) / Inria Willow (Crocoddyl), Unitree, Berkeley

nodes.What it is: Contacts (feet, fingers, collisions) make dynamics discontinuous: forces appear suddenly. Simulators approximate contact with solvers or soft penalties. Differentiable simulators also return gradients of the outcome with respect to actions or parameters, for optimization and system identification.
nodes.Prerequisites: Rigid-body dynamics; autodiff/JAX or PyTorch; GPUs
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MuJoCo Warp (DeepMind + NVIDIA, Newton project) runs MuJoCo on GPUs; its README says differentiability is not yet available (tracked in issue #500). DiffMJX (2025) shows hard-contact gradients are biased and proposes fixes. Gradient quality through contact is still an open problem.
nodes.Key players: Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, academic groups (DiffMJX: Paulus, Geist, Martius et al.)

nodes.What it is: Retargeting converts human motion capture or video into joint trajectories for a robot with different proportions and joint limits. It is solved with IK plus constraints against foot sliding and self-collision. The result is the reference motion that RL tracking policies learn to imitate.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: GMR (2025) shows retargeting quality directly limits policy robustness and supports 15+ humanoids including Unitree G1 and Berkeley Humanoid Lite; BeyondMimic trains dynamic skills (cartwheels, sprints) from retargeted LAFAN1 data.
nodes.Key players: Stanford (C. Karen Liu), UC Berkeley (Sreenath), Unitree

robots_models.Name: Pinocchio
robots_models.Key specs: C++ template library with Python bindings; RNEA/ABA with analytical derivatives, centroidal dynamics, regressors for identification, closed-loop and frictional contact support
robots_models.Why it matters: Paris-built reference library for robot dynamics; foundation of Crocoddyl and Pink.

robots_models.Name: Featherstone spatial_v2
robots_models.Key specs: MATLAB implementation of spatial-vector rigid-body dynamics algorithms
robots_models.Why it matters: Reference implementation accompanying the standard dynamics algorithms book.

robots_models.Name: Robotics Toolbox for Python
robots_models.Key specs: Elementary transform sequences, fkine, Jacobians, Hessians, manipulability, numerical IK
robots_models.Why it matters: Gentlest Python entry to kinematics for beginners.

robots_models.Name: TRAC-IK
robots_models.Key specs: Runs KDL Newton (with random restarts) and SQP solvers concurrently; handles joint limits; time-bounded solves
robots_models.Why it matters: Robust generic IK drop-in for KDL used in ROS/MoveIt setups.

robots_models.Name: mink
robots_models.Key specs: QP differential IK on MuJoCo models: frame, CoM, posture tasks; joint, velocity and collision limits; floating base
robots_models.Why it matters: Fastest way to make any MuJoCo robot (arm or humanoid) follow targets; used by retargeting tools.

robots_models.Name: Pink
robots_models.Key specs: Weighted-task QP differential IK on Pinocchio models with configuration and velocity limits
robots_models.Why it matters: Pinocchio-based counterpart of mink; good for URDF-first stacks.

robots_models.Name: Ruckig
robots_models.Price / access: Community version free (MIT), pip; Pro version paid
robots_models.Key specs: Jerk-limited, time-optimal state-to-state trajectories in real time (cycle times down to 250 µs per vendor site)
robots_models.Why it matters: Makes any arm move smoothly with a few lines of code; integrated in MoveIt.

robots_models.Name: TOPP-RA
robots_models.Key specs: Time-optimal path parameterization by reachability analysis, O(mN), robust
robots_models.Why it matters: Standard method to traverse a given path as fast as joint limits allow.

robots_models.Name: Crocoddyl
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): RoMI Lab (Heriot-Watt, Edinburgh Centre for Robotics), LAAS-CNRS Gepetto, Inria Willow (loco-3d)
robots_models.Key specs: DDP-family optimal control solvers (FDDP etc.) for contact sequences; uses Pinocchio derivatives
robots_models.Why it matters: French-origin reference for whole-body trajectory optimization of humanoids and quadrupeds.

robots_models.Name: MuJoCo Warp
robots_models.Price / access: Free; needs NVIDIA GPU for speed
robots_models.Key specs: GPU-accelerated MuJoCo for NVIDIA hardware; maintained by Google DeepMind and NVIDIA (Newton project); differentiability via Warp not yet available per README (issue #500)
robots_models.Why it matters: Massively parallel contact simulation for RL and sysid.

robots_models.Name: DiffMJX
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Paulus, Geist, Schumacher, Musil, Rappenecker, Martius (arXiv 2506.14186)
robots_models.Key specs: Adaptive time integration + 'contacts from distance' to improve gradients through hard contacts in MuJoCo XLA
robots_models.Why it matters: Explains why naive gradients through contact are wrong, a key pitfall for differentiable sim projects.

robots_models.Name: MuJoCo Menagerie
robots_models.Key specs: Curated MJCF models of arms, quadrupeds (Go2, Spot, ANYmal) and humanoids (G1 29-DoF, H1, Booster T1, ToddlerBot)
robots_models.Why it matters: Ready-to-simulate robot models: no need to author a description first.

robots_models.Name: onshape-to-robot
robots_models.Price / access: Free, pip; needs Onshape account/API key
robots_models.Key specs: Exports Onshape assemblies to URDF, SDF or MuJoCo; dof_/frame_/closing_ mate naming conventions
robots_models.Why it matters: Closes the gap between student CAD and a simulatable robot model.

robots_models.Name: BAM (Better Actuator Models)
robots_models.Key specs: Extended friction models (Stribeck, load-dependence) M1-M6; pre-identified Dynamixel MX-64/MX-106/XL-320/XL330, eRob80 and Feetech STS3215; MuJoCo and MuJoCo Warp/mjlab integration; pendulum identification bench
robots_models.Why it matters: Directly targets low-cost servo sim-to-real, our likely hardware class.

robots_models.Name: BIRDy
robots_models.Key specs: Benchmark of 17 inertial identification methods incl. physically consistent SDP variants; excitation trajectory tools
robots_models.Why it matters: Reference benchmark to pick an identification method.

robots_models.Name: GMR (General Motion Retargeting)
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Stanford (Araujo, Ze, Xu, Wu, C. Karen Liu)
robots_models.Key specs: Real-time retargeting from SMPL-X/BVH/FBX to 15+ humanoids incl. Unitree G1 (29 DoF) and Berkeley Humanoid Lite
robots_models.Why it matters: State-of-the-art open retargeter; reduces artifacts that break RL tracking.

robots_models.Name: BeyondMimic
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): UC Berkeley / Stanford (Liao, Truong, Huang, Tevet, Sreenath, Liu)
robots_models.Price / access: Motion-tracking training code public (MIT per mirror repo); full stack availability not verified
robots_models.Key specs: RL motion tracking of retargeted LAFAN1 motions plus guided diffusion policy for zero-shot tasks
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows how good retargeted kinematics become dynamic real-robot skills.

robots_models.Name: Unitree G1
robots_models.Price / access: Price from $13.5K (vendor page); EDU variant priced separately
robots_models.Key specs: Humanoid; 29-DoF MJCF in Menagerie; base and EDU versions
robots_models.Why it matters: Most common low-cost research humanoid target for retargeting and whole-body control.

robots_models.Name: Low-cost 3D-printed delta robot (IJMERR 2024)
robots_models.Price / access: Open-source 3D-printed parts; total cost not stated in source
robots_models.Key specs: 3 servos, Arduino Uno; 2.2 mm accuracy, 0.4 m/s, 30 picks/min, 200 g payload (paper)
robots_models.Why it matters: Concrete cheap parallel robot with documented IK/FK and trajectory planning.

top3.justification: Highest reuse: the same QP-IK code powers teleop, retargeting and humanoid reach; free in sim, very visual (phone-pose teleop), and the tools (mink/Pink) are maintained by active open-source authors.
Software-only, public data and code, and a very filmable result (a humanoid doing your dance); directly feeds the 2025-26 humanoid learning wave. Real-robot execution is expensive, so keep it in sim.

Cheapest lever on the robot-learning-on-low-cost-hardware hypothesis: a servo bench costs little, and BAM (Rhoban, Bordeaux) already ships a Feetech STS3215 model that we can validate on the SO-101 and feed back to the LeRobot community.
